<p align="center">
  <b>CASTAWAY</b> <i>(working title)</i>: ten golden hours on one tiny island.<br>
  She nods to the music. Every so often, something happens. The sun stays exactly where it is.
</p>

<p align="center">
  <kbd>RUNTIME</kbd> 10:00:00 &nbsp;·&nbsp; <kbd>TEMPO</kbd> 80 BPM &nbsp;·&nbsp; <kbd>KEY</kbd> F&nbsp;major &nbsp;·&nbsp; <kbd>SEED</kbd> 1992 &nbsp;·&nbsp; <kbd>SUNSETS COMPLETED</kbd> 0
</p>

A stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. It is an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of *Johnny Castaway*, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, repainted as a sunny, hand-painted coastal anime scene: 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, and always daytime. The banner up there is the synthwave cover version, and even there the sun has been told to hold.

Mostly she idles. [activities.toml](activities.toml) puts more than 90 activities on four timers, from a coconut every few minutes to a walk across the sea for an iced coffee once in a very long while, and she is busy about a third of the time. Every activity waits for the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds, so even the gags land on the beat. Every sound, from the kalimba theme to the waves, is synthesized from code by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py).

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

Live preview in the page, then export a YouTube-ready MP4: the browser encodes frame-exact H.264 with WebCodecs (68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), and the server mixes in the sound and joins the two. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages.


A selection, as of 2026-10-01: the file lists more than 90 activities and other sessions keep adding to it. Each length is the range in [activities.toml](activities.toml), picked fresh every time; the counts are the medians of 200 simulated 10-hour runs, as the file's own header says. Follow-ups never come round on a timer: the tide only arrives after a sandcastle, and the reply only after her bottle washes straight back. `python tools/schedule.py` validates the file and simulates a run of its own; `python tools/render_demo.py --dev` renders a reel of every activity with a heads-up display.

Each timer picks by weight among what is free right now. Lanes let things overlap, so a ship can sail past while she is busy with a coconut, and it even waits for her to get busy. Also on the record, all real: bushcraft (fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing), waving for rescue, and a kumara she plants in the sand that grows over the course of the video. Under it all runs the scene life: 26 entries, of which the shore waves and the drifting cloud shadows are built so far; birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and one rain shower are planned.

```text
 LINER NOTES
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

                   20 bars of exactly 3 s: electric piano, a kalimba
                   lead, soft drums, vinyl hiss and ticks
 OCEAN ........... a seamless 60 s loop of its own
 EVERYTHING ELSE . more than 150 sound files, made the same way
 SOURCE .......... tools/make_audio.py. no samples, no loops, no
                   recordings, so no third-party licence applies
 MASTERED ........ -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP; levels for
                   the master and for each routine
 HEARD BY ........ nobody, yet
```

The banner keeps the same time. The floor moves one grid line per beat (0.75 s at 80 BPM), a new slit starts down the sun on every bar (3 s), her head and the shark's nod once a beat, and the whole story is twelve bars long. It would all be on the beat, if images could make a sound. Source: [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>HOW THE SUN IS HELD UP</b>: the banner, taken apart</summary>

The genre's sun is always setting. This one cannot: the project has a rule that it is always daytime. So it does the next best thing. Six dark slits slide down its lower half, one starting every bar, each growing from under half a pixel to about ten as it reaches the base, which is exactly what a setting sun looks like in this style. The disc itself does not move a pixel. It has been setting since 0:00:00 and it will still be setting at 10:00:00.

The rest, back to front:

- **Sky and clouds.** A dusk-purple gradient and, where the genre puts low-poly mountains, low-poly cumulus: overlapping puffs, their outline zipped into big triangles and lit from below and from the sun's side, the way sunset clouds are. They float a few pixels clear of the horizon, because clouds do.
- **The sea.** A magenta wireframe floor: a fixed fan of lines to the vanishing point and thirty cross lines that all run the same 22.5-second track toward the viewer, one beat apart, with keyframes picked so every straight step stays within 0.35 px of true perspective. Under the sun, its reflection flickers between two sets of broken bars on the beat.
- **The island.** One palm (a curved, tapering trunk and nine drooping fronds with a fringe of leaflets), a raft that bobs, a ring of foam every bar, and her: flat shapes with a dark outline, a nod on every beat and a sip of iced coffee twice a loop.
- **The story.** Twelve bars, 36 seconds. A shark in headphones crosses and nods with her. At 0:12 she turns round and walks out over the water to the vanishing point, stepping twice a beat and shrinking as she goes. The hydrofoil crosses while she is away, and he throws his shaka at a palm. At 0:22.5 she reappears at the vanishing point and walks back with a fresh one. In the video, when he comes by, she jumps up, runs over and waves, and he waves back. The banner is the only place she has missed him.
- **The word.** Eight heavy, rounded-square capitals drawn as thick stroked centrelines, skewed 13 degrees, filled with a chrome gradient that has one hard stop for the horizon, then outlined, extruded seven steps down and to the right, and glowed with wider, fainter copies. The shine is a soft white bar masked to the letter faces.
- **The brush lettering.** *golden hours* is a spline through hand-placed points, swept by a broad nib held at 38 degrees, so the strokes go thick and thin like a brush, then given a neon glow and a dark drop shadow. It flickers on once when the page loads.

No text elements, no fonts and no filters: every glow is a wider, fainter copy of the same line. One 106 KB SVG with CSS keyframes, regenerated by a dependency-free Node generator. With reduced motion set, it holds a complete frame: her by the palm with the coffee, the shark mid-sea, every word drawn.

</details>

Castaway is an unofficial project inspired by the 1992 screensaver *Johnny Castaway*, which belongs to its owners; it is not affiliated with them. Synthwave is a style reference only: no real logo, film title, game, record sleeve or typeface is reproduced, and all art here is original. The Sunset Extension Bureau, Vanishing Point Coffee Co. and Low Horizon Tapes are made up.
